column1: # Decisions of qualification/hash-reentrant-guard-20261107 (open items S1 and S2 of #2676). Measured before designing: M3HashReentrantLookupSelfTest report mode on the base (#2676 head 0b97282f6d1d) with the java.util twin of every owner as the reference column (REFERENCE.tsv; one case per user-callback call N; actions: clear + re-insert 50/60, and for operations on a new key 9 a callback that inserts key 9 itself). Verdicts: BEFORE/AFTER = linearizable (callback's change first / operation first), FAILFAST = CME with the callback's content, WRONG = neither, DAMAGED = owner invariants or map consistency broken. Rule from the brief: never stricter than the JDK where its contract allows the behaviour, unless the M3 owner would otherwise be damaged (broken invariants or a wrong mapping removed); the test encodes it (M3 FAILFAST only where the twin is not cleanly linearizable; M3 WRONG only on a read where the twin is WRONG too; never DAMAGED).

column3: BEFORE 99, AFTER 55, FAILFAST 4, WRONG 8, DAMAGED 57 (reads answer the pre-change value; mutating operations re-link a bin of the cleared table: size/lookup inconsistent)
column7: base WRONG: get/getOrDefault return v60 for key 2 (a foreign mapping, which no java.util owner returns); remove/keySet.remove/entrySet.remove/compute(remove)/merge(remove)/remove(k,v) erase key 60 (wrong mapping removed); put(existing)/replace/replace(k,old,new)/computeIfPresent/compute(write)/merge(write) write key 60; putIfAbsent/computeIfAbsent/compute/merge on a new key lose the callback's racing insert (the absent path looked the key up again through put). DAMAGED: remove(6) erases a released slot ('index count'). Head: 0 WRONG, 0 DAMAGED; FAILFAST only values.remove (iterator CME), where HashMap fails fast too
column8: find walks again when the key's equals changed the structure (bounded by M3SlotMap.REWALKS = 8, then CME); put = find + insertNew; locate/insertAbsent for the read-modify-write operations

column7: same WRONG shapes; DAMAGED remove(6) ('hash size'). Needs the m3_arrays JNI library: measured with libm3_arrays.dll built from m3/arrays/src/main/native (MinGW + CMake); the default Maven run skips the linked owners and names them
plus get(6): access order moves a released slot ('hash links'); a re-walk caused by the owner's own move is harmless (the next walk finds the key)
plus DAMAGED duplicate key 9 in put/putIfAbsent/computeIfAbsent/compute/merge on a new key: put called hashCode a second time after its lookup and inserted without looking again
column8: find walks again (same bound); put hashes the key once (find + insertNew), like WeakHashMap; locate/insertAbsent

column7: set.remove erases key 60; set.remove(6) erases a released slot; set.add's absent path stays findSlot + put (its outcomes are linearizable: a racing add makes it AFTER)

column2: every slot-map owner (M3SlotMap bodies): remove(k,v), replace(k,old,new), entrySet().remove
column3: java.util: HashMap.remove(k,v) DAMAGED/WRONG under value-equals mutation; replace(k,old,new) on WeakHashMap WRONG
column4: base WRONG (wrong mapping removed or written: the value's equals released the slot, eraseAt/writeAt hit the reused one)
column7: value equals is a user callback between the lookup and the write; mutants SM-1/SM-2 (no look-again) are killed
column8: the operation looks the key up again when the value's equals changed the structure (same bound), so it acts on the post-change state; entrySet().contains/containsValue are reads and stay as they are (their outcomes are linearizable)

column7: compute/merge/computeIfAbsent write a present key through its slot instead of putting it again: one comparator walk instead of two, as java.util.TreeMap's compute; the absent path still puts (insertAbsent default), guarded by #2676

column5: M3 FAILFAST only in values.remove (iterator CME) on every owner, where the twin fails fast as well
column7: a disturbed walk is repeated, not refused: mutant SM-9 (REWALKS = 0, refuse at once) is killed by the strictness rule (get would fail fast where HashMap answers); the bound only stops a key whose equals changes the map at every call

column2: insertAbsent precondition (revision equals the one locate returned to)
column7: every caller proves it first (no user code in between, or check(expected)); mutants HM-2/LH-2/WH-3 survive by design

M3IntIntHashMap and the other primitive M3*HashMap owners (held by another agent), M3TransientFacadeStore; M3WeakHashMap's drain of GC-cleared keys is a nonstructural erase that a callback-triggered lookup could run without a revision change (not reproducible deterministically; noted, not guarded)

BENCH.tsv: paired base/head rounds in one JVM (two class loaders), with an A/A run as the noise band; a first loop shape (an outer retry loop around the walk) measured Integer get-hit 1.14 and put-overwrite 1.20 x base, so the walk keeps its original shape and only the hash-equal branch gained one revision compare, the re-walk being a separate cold method
column8: find(key, hash) -> find(key, hash, walks) + rewalk
